text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert — elevated 503s observed from ELB pool in eu-west-3 (azf). 503 rate to edge proxies spiked to 18% over last 5m. Alert ID: ELB-503-578123.

sarah: paging oncall_nw — can you grab? customers reporting timeouts and failed prompts.

oncall_nw: on it, joining. What metrics do we have?

mike: seeing targetgroup unhealthy count jump on tg-web-azf by ~40% starting 5781233700. Connection reset and 502->503. Logs showing backend 504s then ELB returning 503.

priya: FWIW, route53 health checks for eu-west-3 edge show high failure rate — likely multi-az traffic bounce. Noticed elevated RTT to AZF collector.

lee: I've started correlation: EBS volume detach errors in azf-1 correlated with spikes, some hosts reporting increased disk IO wait. Could be EC2 host-level flapping.

oncall_nw: ok — triage plan: 1) isolate azf ELBs and shift traffic away via weighted Route53, 2) mark tg-web-azf as draining, 3) kickoff host remediation. Who can run the shift?

sarah: I can do a quick Route53 weight change to reduce region weight to 0.2 for eu-west-3 and increase eu-west-1 to compensate. Deploy-bot, prepare for potential scale up in eu-west-1?

deploy-bot: auto-suggest: scale web-cluster in eu-west-1 by +30% to absorb influx. Manual confirm required.

jordan: confirming scaling now — starting autoscaling policy override. ETA ~3m for warm instances.

mike: meanwhile blocking rule applied on tg-web-azf: set desired instances to draining=true and deregistration delay set to 10s.

oncall_nw: good. Sarah — go ahead with Route53 weight adjustment and post exact change.

sarah: doing it now: https://console.aws.amazon.com/route53/hostedzones/Z123456 — changed weights: eu-west-3 -> 10, eu-west-1 -> 90 at 5781234120.

incident-bot: Route53 update detected by infra-audit at 5781234123 (user: sarah).

priya: Observability — latency at edge drops within ~45s of route53 change, 503 rate reduces to 4% but still above baseline. Some clients still hitting azf nodes due to DNS TTL.

lee: Host side: found EC2 kernel logs showing ENA NIC flaps on a subset of instances in azf-1 starting 5781233600. Also one EBS volume exhibiting io timeouts; support ticket opened with AWS (case 987654321).

oncall_nw: AWS contact?

mike: AWS replied initial triage: "Investigating possible networking hardware issue in AZF networking fabric; isolation measures in progress."

jordan: I've kicked an emergency drain for all web nodes in azf-1 and attached a temporary NAT path to avoid egress blackhole.

priya: Customer impact assessment: ~12% of API requests (by token volume) during spike window affected with 503s. Top impacted customers: internal staging clusters and 3 paying customers experiencing user-facing errors. Sending preliminary incident email to CS and support.

sarah: Drafting message: "We're seeing degraded service in eu-west-3 affecting some traffic. We're shifting traffic and remediating hosts. More updates in 30m." Anyone want to add details?

lee: Add that AWS is engaged and we've opened a support case; include guidance to temporarily retry or route to eu-west-1.

oncall_nw: Setting oncall escalation to next level if we don't get AWS confirmation in 20m. Priya, can you monitor DNS TTL/proxy caches?

priya: Watching — caches show gradual TTL decay, expect final detachment of traffic from azf by ~6m given client caches.

mike: Patchwork fix: for affected EBS, detached and re-attached one volume in azf-1 host-17; host recovered but still under observation.

incident-bot: Pager rotation: primary oncall_nw -> sarah (handoff) at 5781235400.

jordan: handoff acknowledged. I'll remain in the channel until stable.

priya: 5781236000 update: 503 rate down to 1.2%, latency baseline restored for most traffic. Customers still hitting old DNS entries see intermittent 503s.

mike: AWS update: "We completed hardware path remediation in AZF; monitoring for recurrence." Ticket updated 5781236320.

lee: Post-incident actions noted: 1) tighten Route53 failover TTLs for eu-west-3 to 30s, 2) add ENA NIC flapping alarms per-host, 3) expand autoscaling warm pool in eu-west-1/2.

sarah: Agreed. I've created a follow-up doc and linked it to the incident tracker: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INC-578123.

oncall_nw: Closing notes: customer impact moderate, mitigation applied via DNS weight shift and host drains. Continuing to monitor for 2 hours, will open a proper postmortem with timeline and RCA.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated at 5781237350. Please label channel thread with "postmortem-required" if you will author RCA.

jordan: tagging for postmortem — I'll take ownership of timeline and network analysis.

sarah: thanks all. :thumbsup:
